observations.title: Breath release
observations.text: With the breath, held knots let go. The release can be broad (many at once, across the body) or focused (one region). Easy knots go within a breath or two; hard ones over many breaths, or not at all. The ability grows with practice.
observations.note: How the breath acts is left open: drive, movement, local nerves, attention, chemistry are variants, not assumptions.

observations.title: Pressure, then release
observations.text: Sustained local pressure for tens of seconds, then release, lets a knot go, faster than calm alone.
observations.note: Reactive hyperaemia after pressure is measured (M); the knot's release is self-report.

observations.title: Attention
observations.text: Focus alone, without pressure or movement, can let a knot go.
observations.note: To define with the author; may belong to O1's focused release.

observations.title: Water
observations.text: Hydration lowers the threshold for release, or speeds it.
observations.note: Most theories are expected to be silent; silence is reported as silence.

observations.title: Stress
observations.text: Sustained stress raises the number of held knots, most where tone is highest: neck and shoulders, jaw, belly, low back.

observations.title: Stiffness
observations.text: Held knots reduce range of motion; a stretch meets them as a dull block.

observations.title: Sparks
observations.text: Release brings a brief tingle over the knot's own patch of skin.
observations.note: Must be spatial: overbreathing makes tingling anywhere, so only tingling confined to the released patch tells theories apart.

observations.title: Migration and the queue
observations.text: Releasing one knot changes others: some let go, some appear; the territory evens out; at some places knots are released and then replaced by others, as if from a queue.

observations.title: A parent releases its children
observations.text: Releasing one knot (a parent) lets many others (its children) go with it.
observations.note: The author's own experience, written down on 26 Sep 2026 after the tree simulation had been shared: the model's match is found after the fact, not predicted blind. How many, how soon, where and what stays are the blind tests.

observations.title: Clusters in place
observations.text: Knots gather in clusters at particular places, the base of the skull most of all; an old, heavily loaded cluster can let go with a wave of warmth spreading from the site.

observations.title: Sizes and numbers
observations.text: Knots come in a hierarchy: a handful of roots at the ridges, big knots that take sessions to clear, and micro knots at dozens per square inch, hundreds of thousands in a body by practitioners' own estimate.
observations.note: The number and density are part of the test: each theory predicts its own, and only a unit that dense can host a micro knot.

observations.title: Mirroring
observations.text: Releasing on one side increases release or range of motion on the other.
observations.note: The crossover effect of stretching one side is measured; a scoping review puts it down most likely to reduced pain perception.

observations.title: Age
observations.text: Knots accumulate with age: young ones small and transient, old ones large and persistent.

observations.title: Euphoria
observations.text: A large release can bring a wave of euphoria.
observations.note: Out of scope for tissue-level models.

observations.title: Peeling and filling
observations.text: Layers of the fascia peel apart along lines, leaving hollows that fill over days.
